name: THX
author: Thomas Nokielski

provenance.from: AMOSTools/Extensions, out of aminet dev/amos/amostools.i386-aros.lha -- held in the corpus at sources/aminet-dev-amos/. Its author's README says the directory is "every AMOS extension I can find, cut down to just their token tables with the make_extensions.pl script", and names the ExoticA AMOS extensions wiki page as the list it works from.
provenance.redistribution: Not redistributed here as software: the file carries no code at all. It is a token table with the library stripped out from under it, kept for identification and detokenising.
provenance.note: ExoticA's AMOS extensions list places it at slot 20. Nothing here observes it in a program: the slot is the wiki's recommendation and no more.

notes: TABLE ONLY. This is an AMOSTools stub -- the hunk shell and the token table survive, both length fields read zero, there is no code, and every entry's two routine words are overwritten with `====`. So the NAMES, the parameter SPECS and, because an id is the byte offset of its entry, the IDS are the original library's; the behaviour is not here and the evidence tier cannot rise above `manual` until a real binary turns up. The reader is checked against CRAFT and MusiCRAFT, which are held both ways, and agrees with them entry for entry -- see parseAmosToolsTable in src/tokens/libtok.ts. Six keywords over a THX/AHX replayer: `thx load`, `thx play`, `thx stop`, `thx volume`, `=thx subsongs`, `=thx end`. NOT THE SAME EXTENSION AS JOTRE, which is also a THX shim and is registered at slot 22 with five keywords of its own spelling (`jolly *`), and not the same as DOOM Music 2.0, which spells all six of these names in its `thx` block. This one shares no ID with DME -- the names are a coincidence of what the format is called. `thx play` here takes two arguments where DME's takes one.
